newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mar wholesale inventories rose 0.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mar wholesale inventories rose 0.7 pct.

text.p: wholesale inventories and sales, seasonally adjusted.
(Billions of dollars) Mar Feb--Rev from Mar96
(Billions of dollars) Mar Feb--Rev from Mar96
Wall Street economists had forecast March wholesale inventories to rise 0.4 percent.
The March stock-to-sales ratio for merchant wholesalers, seasonally adjusted, rose to 1.24 months' worth from 1.22 months' worth in February.
The ratio is a measure of how many months it would take to sell existing inventories at the current sales pace.
The department had revised February wholesale trade data in its annual benchmark revisions issued May 6.
The 0.9 percent drop in March wholesale sales was the largest monthly decline since a 1.2 percent drop last August, it said.

Beginning with the March report, the department said it changed the sample base for its monthly survey and the sample design it uses to collect the data. The changes should reduce the number of revisions, it said.
The new survey sample canvases approximately 3,800 firms, the same number as before, but requires them to report sales and inventories each month rather than every three months, Commerce said.
